headline: Govt to merge 3 investment agencies to boost foreign investment
summary: The 'Invest Bangladesh Act, 2026' will create a single authority to simplify approvals and registration, aiming to improve the country's FDI position.
details: The government has finalised the draft 'Invest Bangladesh Act, 2026', which will merge the Bangladesh Investment Development Authority (BIDA), Bangladesh Economic Zones Authority (BEZA), and Public-Private Partnership Authority (PPPA) into a single entity.
This move aims to simplify the process of receiving services, registration, and import-export for investors through a modern one-stop service and digitalised approval processes.
The decision comes after a UN report showed Bangladesh's ability to attract foreign direct investment (FDI) was lower than that of countries like Uganda and Ghana, despite having a larger economy.
A powerful new authority will be led by an individual with ministerial rank, with ministers of trade and investment-related ministries serving as members to speed up decision-making.
Additionally, the cabinet approved the 'National Renewable Energy Development Strategy 2026-2030', targeting 20% electricity from renewable sources by 2030.
The energy strategy focuses on rooftop solar, wind, hydropower, and EV charging, while ensuring at least 30% female participation in renewable energy technology training.
The cabinet also approved the draft 'Import Policy Order 2026-2029' to modernise trade procedures and further facilitate investment.
caption:
Bangladesh is merging three major investment agencies into one to stop losing foreign investment to smaller economies.

The government has finalised the draft 'Invest Bangladesh Act, 2026', which will merge the Bangladesh Investment Development Authority (BIDA), Bangladesh Economic Zones Authority (BEZA), and Public-Private Partnership Authority (PPPA) into a single entity.

This move aims to simplify the process of receiving services, registration, and import-export for investors through a modern one-stop service and digitalised approval processes.

The decision comes after a UN report showed Bangladesh's ability to attract foreign direct investment (FDI) was lower than that of countries like Uganda and Ghana, despite having a larger economy.

A powerful new authority will be led by an individual with ministerial rank, with ministers of trade and investment-related ministries serving as members to speed up decision-making.

Additionally, the cabinet approved the 'National Renewable Energy Development Strategy 2026-2030', targeting 20% electricity from renewable sources by 2030.

The energy strategy focuses on rooftop solar, wind, hydropower, and EV charging, while ensuring at least 30% female participation in renewable energy technology training.

The cabinet also approved the draft 'Import Policy Order 2026-2029' to modernise trade procedures and further facilitate investment.

headline: US hits 90 targets as US-Iran ceasefire crumbles
summary: New fighting erupts as the US strikes Iranian military sites and Tehran targets US allies in the region, ending a short-lived peace accord.
details: New fighting has erupted between the United States and Iran, effectively ending a ceasefire from April and a subsequent accord in June. The hostilities were triggered by tensions over the Strait of Hormuz, a vital oil and gas corridor.

The US military reported hitting approximately 90 Iranian military targets, including air defence systems and missile and drone storage sites. Iranian officials stated that these strikes killed 17 people.
In retaliation, Iran targeted US assets in Kuwait, Bahrain, and Qatar. Jordan's military also intercepted eight missiles launched from Iran, while Iran hit at least three ships in recent days.
The escalation comes as Iran prepares to bury its supreme leader, Ali Khamenei, who was killed on February 28. Crowds in Mashhad have called for vengeance against the US and Israel.

US President Donald Trump has declared the ceasefire 'over,' though he remains open to talks. Meanwhile, Israel's Defence Minister warned that Israel is prepared to attack Iran a 'third time' if necessary.
The conflict has severely impacted maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, with shipping volumes falling sharply after vessels were attacked earlier this week.
